stem:
Which one out of the following sets of diagrams correctly depicts reproduction in Amoeba and Yeast? (Each option is a set of two labelled diagrams. The correct set must show an irregular Amoeba whose nucleus elongates and the cell splits into two daughter amoebae under the label 'Binary fission in Amoeba', and a rounded Yeast cell growing a small bud under the label 'Budding in Yeast'.)

Option a): a budding-yeast diagram wrongly labelled 'Binary fission in Amoeba' (top) and a budding-yeast diagram labelled 'Budding in Yeast' (bottom).
Option b): an Amoeba splitting into two wrongly labelled 'Budding in Amoeba' (top) and a budding yeast wrongly labelled 'Binary fission in Yeast' (bottom).
Option c): a budding yeast wrongly labelled 'Binary fission in Yeast' (bottom), with mismatched labels.
Option d): an Amoeba with elongating nucleus splitting into two daughters correctly labelled 'Binary fission in Amoeba' (top), and a yeast cell growing a bud correctly labelled 'Budding in Yeast' (bottom).

The given graph shows the hormonal changes during a normal menstrual cycle. What would be a likely consequence if the hormone represented by Q in the given graph is lacking in an adult female?

(The figure is a graph of hormone 'Level in blood' versus 'Days'. Curve P starts moderate, dips, then rises to a sharp peak exactly at the dotted line marked 'Ovulation occurs' (about day 14) and then falls — it surges at ovulation. Curve Q stays near zero before ovulation and only begins to rise steadily AFTER ovulation, staying elevated through the later part of the cycle.)

options.label: A
options.text: Levels of the hormone represented by graph P would be higher than normal.

options.label: B
options.text: Fertilisation of ovum would fail to occur.

options.label: C
options.text: There would be no significant effect since the functions of the hormones overlap.

options.label: D
options.text: The uterine lining might not be sufficiently stable for implantation of fertilised ovum.

stem: The organism in which an outgrowth on the parent body develops into a new individual is:

Choose the correct order of the stages of binary fission in Leishmania.

(The figure shows five outlines of a slender Leishmania cell labelled I–V. In I the cell has a single rounded nucleus; in II the single nucleus has divided into two nuclei; in III the cell carries two nuclei and is starting to elongate; in IV the elongated cell is constricting/separating into two; in V two fully separate daughter cells are seen.)

The diagram given below illustrates

(The figure shows a single irregular Amoeba-shaped cell whose nucleus has stretched into an elongated dumb-bell shape across the middle of the cell, the stage just before the cell divides into two.)

options.label: B
options.text: formation of daughter cells in Yeast

stem:
The budding in Yeast is illustrated by the diagram:

(Four diagrams are given as options. Diagram A is a cell with a central partition splitting it into two equal halves. Diagram B is a plain rounded cell with no division. Diagram C is an oval cell with a central partition dividing it into two equal halves. Diagram D is an oval cell with a small bud growing out from one side.)

The following are the sketches made by some students. The sketch NOT illustrative of budding in yeast is:

(Four circular microscope-field sketches A–D. Sketch A shows a chain of cells with attached buds. Sketch B shows a chain of cells with attached buds. Sketch C shows several scattered, separate oval cells with no buds attached to one another. Sketch D shows cells with buds attached.)

Which part of the following produce egg?

(The figure is a labelled diagram of the human female reproductive system. Label A points to the central body of the uterus; label B points to the fallopian tube/oviduct at the top; label C points to the grainy oval ovary at the side; label D points to the vagina at the bottom.)

Which one of the following sketches does not illustrate budding in Yeast?

(Four sketches labelled I–IV. Sketch I is a mother yeast cell with a small bud and bud-nucleus forming at the top. Sketch II is a yeast cell whose nucleus is stretching into a forming bud. Sketch III shows three separate, individual cells each with its own nucleus, not joined by any bud. Sketch IV is a mother cell with an attached bud.)

A student observed a slide of Yeast under a microscope and saw a collection of cells in different parts of the slide marked A, B, C and D as shown below. Which one of the following parts of the slide shows budding in yeast?

(The figure is a circular microscope field divided into four quadrants: D (top-left) and A (top-right) show scattered separate oval cells; C (bottom-left) shows a short chain of cells; B (bottom-right) shows cells each bearing an attached bud forming small chains.)

Two of the following four figures that illustrate budding are:

(Four figures labelled I–IV. Figure I is a chain of rounded yeast cells with attached buds. Figure II is an upright fungal structure with a slender stalk, a knob bearing spores at the top and root-like rhizoids at the base (a spore-producing mould). Figure III is a plant with a horizontal runner/stem from which new plantlets arise (vegetative propagation). Figure IV is a Bryophyllum leaf bearing small buds (plantlets) along its margin.)

Four stages of binary fission in Amoeba are shown below. The stage at which nuclear fission and cytokinesis are observed is stage

(Four diagrams labelled I–IV. Stage I shows two fully separated daughter Amoebae each with a nucleus. Stage II shows a single cell deeply constricted in the middle with the nucleus already split into two halves at opposite ends — both nuclear division and cell (cytokinesis) division occurring together. Stage III shows a cell with an elongated dumb-bell nucleus. Stage IV shows a cell with a single rounded nucleus.)

The process represented in the diagram below is the

(The figure shows a sequence: a single rounded cell with one nucleus, then the nucleus elongates, then the cell constricts in the middle, then two separate daughter cells each with a nucleus are formed.)

options.label: A
options.text: Formation of bud taking place in Amoeba

options.label: C
options.text: identical gametes being formed in Amoeba

options.label: D
options.text: formation of daughter cells in Amoeba

stem:
In which of the following, binary fission observed?

(Four diagrams labelled A–D. A shows a structure with a narrow constriction (a budding/Hydra-like outgrowth). B shows a branching chain of yeast cells with multiple buds. C shows an Amoeba pinched in the middle, dividing into two equal halves. D shows an oval cell/sporangium filled with many small spores.)

Out of the following diagram which one depicts a stage in binary fission of Amoeba?

(Four diagrams labelled A–D. A is a rounded cell with a small bud at the top (budding). B is an undivided irregular amoeboid cell. C is a rounded cell with a small bud (budding). D is a cell constricted in the middle into two equal halves, a figure-of-eight shape — binary fission.)

In the figure of budding in Yeast given above, structures A, B, C and D should be labelled respectively as

(The figure is a budding yeast: a large oval mother cell carrying a small bud at the top. Label A points to a tiny dot (nucleus) inside the small bud; label B points to the small bud itself; label C points to the large mother cell body (the yeast); label D points to the dark nucleus inside the large mother cell.)

options.label: A
options.text: nucleus of bud, bud, yeast, nucleus of yeast

options.label: B
options.text: nucleus of bud, bud, yeast, dividing nucleus of yeast

options.label: C
options.text: dividing nucleus of bud, bud, yeast, nucleus

options.label: D
options.text: dividing nucleus of yeast, yeast, bud, nucleus of bud

stem:
Out of four slides I, II, III, IV whose details are shown below, which one should be focused under the microscope for showing budding in Yeast?

(Four slide sketches labelled I–IV. Slide I shows rounded yeast-type cells, one bearing a small attached bud. Slides II, III and IV all show irregular amoeboid cells with elongating/dividing nuclei (Amoeba binary fission), not rounded budding cells.)

From the following diagrams, select the correct ones showing stages of binary fission in Amoeba and budding in Yeast in their proper sequence.

(Eight numbered diagrams. 1: two separate amoeboid daughter cells. 2: a rounded yeast cell with central nucleus beginning a tiny bud. 3: a yeast cell with an enlarging bud and the nucleus migrating toward it. 4: a rounded cell with an elongated nucleus, constricting. 5: a rounded yeast cell with a small bud bump. 6: a rounded yeast cell with a distinct bud bearing its own nucleus. 7: an amoeboid cell constricted in the middle (figure-of-eight). 8: an amoeboid cell with an elongated dumb-bell nucleus.)

Out of the given diagrams, the correctly labelled diagram showing budding in yeast is:

(Four budding-yeast diagrams labelled I–IV, each a mother cell with a bud. Diagram I labels the bud's contents 'Nuclear fragment' and the body 'Nucleus'. Diagram II labels the bud 'Nucleus of bud' and the body 'Nucleus of Yeast'. Diagram III labels the bud 'Nucleus of mother cell' and the body 'Nucleus of daughter cell'. Diagram IV labels the bud 'Nucleolus of bud' and the body 'Nucleolus of Yeast'.)

Consider the following three flowers namely X, Y and Z. Which flower(s) would develop into a fruit?

(The figure shows longitudinal sections of three flowers. Flower X has both stamens and a central carpel/pistil (a gynoecium with style and stigma in the middle) — bisexual. Flower Y also has a slender central carpel/pistil rising in the middle. Flower Z has only a cluster of parallel stamen-like filaments and no central carpel — it lacks a gynoecium.)

The figures above are drawn from slides showing reproduction in Yeast and Amoeba. The correct description of the above is:

(Two figures. The left figure is an irregular Amoeba-shaped cell whose nucleus has stretched into an elongated dumb-bell across the cell, but the cell itself is not yet constricted. The right figure is a rounded Yeast cell carrying a small bud at the top, the bud already having its own nucleus.)

options.label: A
options.text: Amoeba undergoing cytokinesis and Yeast undergoing budding.

options.label: B
options.text: The nucleus of a parent Amoeba is undergoing division to pass into its bud while Yeast has already divided into two daughter cells.

options.label: C
options.text: Amoeba undergoing binary fission but at a stage when nucleus is elongating, while Yeast has undergone budding.

options.label: D
options.text: Yeast undergoing binary fission and daughter nuclei have already formed, while a newly formed daughter Amoeba is undergoing growth.

stem:
The following figures illustrate binary fission in Amoeba in a correct sequence. The correct sequence is

(Four diagrams labelled (i)–(iv). (i) shows two separate daughter Amoebae each with a nucleus. (ii) shows a single Amoeba with one rounded nucleus. (iii) shows an Amoeba with the nucleus elongating into a dumb-bell. (iv) shows the Amoeba with a fully stretched dumb-bell nucleus and the cell beginning to constrict.)

Which part of the following is a site of implantation?

(The figure is a labelled diagram of the human female reproductive system. Label A points to the central body of the uterus (the dark triangular cavity); label B points to the fallopian tube/oviduct at the top; label C points to the grainy oval ovary at the side; label D points to the vagina at the bottom.)

Slides A and B show stages of asexual reproduction in two different organisms. The slides A and B are depicting

(Slide A shows an irregular Amoeba cell with an elongated dumb-bell nucleus splitting into two daughter Amoebae. Slide B shows a rounded cell with a small bud growing out, the bud carrying a nucleus and separating from the parent.)

options.label: A
options.text: Binary fission in Amoeba and budding in Yeast

options.label: B
options.text: Budding in both Amoeba and Yeast

options.label: C
options.text: Binary fission in Yeast and budding in Amoeba

options.label: D
options.text: Binary fission in both Amoeba and Yeast
